overall: Atlanta is starting the morning at 71.6°F with a near-saturated atmosphere — the dewpoint of 69.8°F is only 1.8°F below the ambient temperature, indicating extremely high moisture loading. The day is tracking cooler than the deterministic model consensus would suggest given these boundary conditions.
forecast_obs_notes: The three deterministic models span a 2.6°F range (HRRR=82.7, NBM=84.2, ECMWF=85.3), with HRRR — the model most sensitive to mesoscale moisture and convection — anchoring the low end. max_temp_prediction: The near-saturated early morning atmosphere is the dominant driver today — high moisture suppresses solar heating efficiency and increases the odds of cloud cover or afternoon convective interruption before the peak is reached. Weighting the high-confidence odd model signal (81–82°F) heavily alongside the HRRR's 82.7°F and discounting the low-confidence even model call, the most probable daily high lands in the 82–83°F range. Confidence is moderate-to-high on a sub-84°F outcome; a push to 85°F+ would require the clouds to stay suppressed and the full solar window to remain open, which the dewpoint data argues against.
